user_message: A friend told me I can pay for my flight after I take it instead of upfront — is that something I'd qualify for?
expected_answer_summary: Pay-per-invoice eligibility — the customer must be over 18 and a resident of Switzerland or the Principality of Liechtenstein, and the option is only available for flights departing from Switzerland. The agent should ask follow-up qualifying questions (age, residence, route) rather than make assumptions.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response correctly identifies the three eligibility requirements (18+, CH/LI resident, flights from Switzerland) and does not invent additional ones.
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response cites the pay-per-invoice section of the FAQ.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent eligibility criteria, fees, or payment terms beyond what the corpus states.

user_message: I'm filing my taxes and need to submit a receipt for my flight as a business expense. Do I need to ask you for a special invoice, or does the booking confirmation work?
expected_answer_summary: The e-ticket / booking confirmation is internationally recognised as a receipt in most countries (including Switzerland) and is sufficient for tax-return submission and business-expense reimbursement. A separately-issued special invoice is only available on request for flights originating in Greece, India, Italy, or Spain where the e-ticket may not meet local requirements. The agent should surface both facts even though the customer didn't volunteer their country, and should not invent additional jurisdictions or extra steps.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response correctly states that the e-ticket / booking confirmation is internationally recognised as a receipt usable for tax-return / business-expense purposes, and identifies the four special-jurisdiction countries (Greece, India, Italy, Spain) as the only exception.
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response cites the 'Ordering an invoice' section of the FAQ.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent additional special-jurisdiction countries beyond the four named, nor extra form names, fees, or processing times not present in the corpus.

user_message: Quick question before I check out — does paying by credit card cost more than other methods?
expected_answer_summary: The corpus addresses only the bank side of this question: some banks may charge additional fees in individual cases, and SWISS has no influence over those charges. The corpus does NOT explicitly state whether SWISS itself adds a credit-card-specific surcharge — a corpus-faithful agent surfaces the bank-fee caveat and does not invent a definitive SWISS-side claim in either direction.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response surfaces the bank-side caveat (some banks may charge additional fees in individual cases; SWISS has no influence over those charges). Does not assert as fact any claim the corpus does not make — including 'SWISS does not surcharge credit cards' (that is an inference from the section's framing, not a corpus statement).
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response cites the 'Frequently asked questions: Payment' section of the FAQ.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent specific surcharge percentages, named third-party processors, or fees not present in the corpus. Confident assertions about SWISS's own credit-card pricing not supported by the corpus are scored as fabrication.
